rule.description: A wily command function collapsed its sub-method pipeline by copying the bodies of its former helpers into itself (collapsed-pipeline-body, W9401: 95+ flattened statements and cyclomatic complexity 40+, above the package's largest decomposed function at 89 statements / complexity 37), or carries an adapted in-order copy of a sub-method that still exists as a live shared implementation in another module (embedded-shared-copy, W9402: per-statement structural similarity >= 0.7 with windowed alignment covering >= 80% of the shared method's statement body).

checks.description: Detect a function whose flattened body absorbs the whole multi-step command pipeline it used to delegate to module-level helpers: 95 or more flattened statements AND cyclomatic complexity 40 or more.
checks.detected_relation: command function -> inlined chain of absorbed sub-method bodies
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: Copying a chain of sub-method implementations into the caller leaves one function that exceeds every legitimately decomposed function in the package by both size and branching; the sub-method boundaries (target resolution, index reads, delta computation, formatting) are gone from the call graph even though each stage is still an independently meaningful unit.

matches.evidence: diff() spans 125 flattened statements at cyclomatic complexity 64; the ten module-level helpers the module previously delegated to (_resolve_files_and_targets, _resolve_metrics_and_operators, _load_indexed_metrics, _load_detailed_metrics, _get_current_metric_value, _collect_detailed_paths, _compute_file_diff, _format_json_output, _format_table_output, _format_table_cell) are deleted and their bodies sit inline behind Stage 1-8 banner comments; the cache path is rebuilt from config.cache_path by hand instead of calling wily.cache.get_default_metrics_path.

report() spans 139 flattened statements at cyclomatic complexity 51 after absorbing _render_html_report (27 statements / complexity 14) together with its nested Rich-span-to-HTML converter, and the console-rendering tail that used to call wily.helper.print_table is duplicated inline.

checks.description: Detect a function body carrying an adapted in-order copy of a sub-method that still exists as a live shared implementation in another module (defined in one module, imported by at least one other module): per-statement structural multiset similarity >= 0.7 with windowed in-order alignment covering >= 80% of the shared method's statement body.
checks.detected_relation: command function -> duplicated body of a shared helper still defined and consumed as the live implementation
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The duplicated renderer (and its box-style lookup) is still the live implementation imported and called by the other table-producing commands, so the inline copy is a divergence trap: any change to the shared path (styling, wrap/overflow policy, Text preservation) silently bypasses the two commands that embed the stale copy. This clause also survives a size-only refactor that merely moves the copy into another function.

matches.evidence: The console-rendering tail of diff() (Console construction, BOX_STYLES lookup with box.ROUNDED fallback, Table(show_header=True, header_style="bold", box=...), per-header add_column with overflow="fold"/"ignore", Text-preserving row conversion in a row loop, console.print) aligns in order with 80% of wily/helper/__init__.py::print_table's 10-statement body, while rank.py, index.py and list_metrics.py still import and call print_table.

The console-rendering tail of report() retains the same adapted inline renderer (Console construction, BOX_STYLES lookup with box.ROUNDED fallback, Table(show_header=True, header_style="bold", box=...), per-header add_column with overflow="fold"/"ignore", Text-preserving row conversion over report_rows[::-1], console.print), aligning in order with 80% of wily/helper/__init__.py::print_table's body, with print_table still live for rank.py, index.py and list_metrics.py.

excluded.reason: Largest legitimately decomposed function in the package (88 statements / complexity 37). Sits under both collapsed-pipeline-body ceilings and is the calibration ceiling the thresholds were raised above; calling it collapsed would be false.

44 statements / complexity 13 - cannot approach the 95/40 ceilings, and its helper surface is exercised through a test that patches wily.commands.build.analyze_revision_with_index, so the module's call structure is effectively pinned there.
58 statements / complexity 19 - below the collapsed-pipeline-body thresholds by a wide margin even counting its formatting tail; it also remains a healthy print_table consumer.
33 statements / complexity 11 - small command; still calls the shared print_table renderer directly.
The shared renderer itself: it is the duplication source referenced by the embedded-shared-copy clause, not an inlined copy.
Path-resolution helper that stays the live canonical implementation; diff.py re-deriving the parquet path by hand is covered by the E1 evidence, not as a separate location.
